home.practice_cutting_blurb: Slice a slab of salvage along its grid and bank the pieces that hold one ore. Big pieces pay far more, and the cuts are few.
cutting.title: Cutting
cutting.how_to: A slab is made of blocks of ore with a few flaws in them. Swipe along a grid line to cut: the cut runs the whole way across the piece it is in and splits it in two. A piece that holds one ore only is banked at once for its size times its size, so one piece of twelve cells pays four times two of six. Each slab comes with a few cuts. When they are spent the rest is scrap, and the slab is graded against the best any plan could have made of it.
cutting.how_to_keyboard: Left and right move a cut that runs down, up and down move one that runs across, tab takes the next piece. Space or enter cuts, escape drops the cut, D gives the slab up.
cutting.tap_note: You can also tap near a line to see the cut, then tap it again to make it. Sides that would be banked light up with what they pay.
cutting.grade_note: All of a slab's best is flawless, four fifths of it is clean. Flawless pays 100 and clean pays 40, times a streak of clean and flawless slabs that climbs to double. A rough slab breaks the streak.
cutting.hint_note: Practice rounds show a cut from a best plan when you pause. The first cut of a good plan often banks nothing.
cutting.legend_ores: Ores: each has its own shape. A flaw is a single cell of the wrong ore in a block.
cutting.legend_cut: A cut runs the whole way across the piece it is made in. A piece of one ore is banked for its size times its size; a mixed piece stays on the table.
cutting.legend_strip: Over the slab: a lamp for each cut left, what you have banked against the slab's best with a notch where clean begins, and the chip that takes the next slab.
harness.preset.cutting_clean_blocks: Clean blocks: no flaws, every cut the slab needs
harness.preset.cutting_tight: Tight: cuts for two thirds of the slab
harness.preset.cutting_busy: Busy from the start: seven blocks, two flaws
harness.preset.cutting_big_slab: A big slab: eight by eight, up to nine cuts
